card.statement:
The Whittaker condition (1.2) is equivalent to the condition

$\displaystyle\bigl(u\eta_{1}+D_{1}\bigr)v_{n+1}(u)=v_{n}(u),$

(2.24)

$\displaystyle D_{d}v_{n}^{(0)}=0,$

(2.25)

$\displaystyle\bigl((q/t)^{d-1}\eta_{d}\Delta_{h_{r-1}}+D_{d}\Delta_{h_{r}}\bigr)v_{n}^{(0)}=0\quad(d\geq 2,\ r\geq 0)$

(2.26)

for each $n\geq 0$.

In the next section we give a proof of these relations. (2.24) is shown in §3.1. In §3.2 we show (2.25). Finally in §3.3 we show (2.26).

3. Proof

3.1. Part 1 of the proof

In this subsection we show the relation

$\displaystyle\bigl(u\eta_{1}+D_{1}\bigr)v_{n+1}(u)=v_{n}(u)$

(3.1)

in Corollary 2.6. Let us introduce a few symbols. For a box $s$ in a Young diagram, the symbols $B_{s}$ is defined to be

$\displaystyle B_{s}=B_{s}(q,t):=q^{j(s)-1}t^{1-i(s)}.$

(3.2)

Thus the alphabet $B_{\lambda}$ defined in (2.6) can be rewritten as

$B_{\lambda}=\{B_{s}\mid s\in\lambda\}.$

We also have

$\displaystyle p_{1}[B_{\lambda}]=e_{1}[B_{\lambda}]=\sum_{s\in\lambda}B_{s}.$

(3.3)

Next we rewrite the Pieri formula [M95, Chap VI, §7] of the Macdonald symmetric function into the following form:

$\displaystyle p_{1}J_{\mu}(q,t)=\sum_{\lambda}J_{\mu}(q,t)d_{\lambda/\mu}(q,t),\qquad d_{\lambda/\mu}(q,t):=\psi^{\prime}_{\lambda/\mu}(q,t)\dfrac{c_{\mu}(q,t)}{c^{\prime}_{\lambda}(q,t)}.$

(3.4)

The running index $\lambda$ runs over the set of partitions such that $|\lambda|=|\mu|+1$ and $\lambda\supset\mu$. See (2.5) for the factor $c^{\prime}_{\lambda}(q,t)$. The factor $\psi^{\prime}_{\lambda/\mu}(q,t)$ is defined by

$\displaystyle\psi^{\prime}_{\lambda/\mu}(q,t):=\prod_{s\in C_{\lambda/\mu}-R_{\lambda/\mu}}\dfrac{b_{\lambda}(s;q,t)}{b_{\mu}(s;q,t)},\qquad b_{\lambda}(s;q,t):=\begin{cases}\dfrac{c_{\lambda}(s;q,t)}{c^{\prime}_{\lambda}(s;q,t)}&s\in\lambda\\
1&s\not\in\lambda\end{cases}.$

(3.5)

Here $C_{\lambda/\mu}$ (resp. $R_{\lambda/\mu}$ ) is the set of columns (resp. rows) that intersect with the boxes in $\lambda/\mu$.

Using the Macdonald inner product (2.3), we also have

$\displaystyle\partial_{p_{1}}J_{\lambda}(q,t)=\sum_{\mu}J_{\mu}(q,t)c_{\lambda/\mu}(q,t),\qquad c_{\lambda/\mu}(q,t):=\psi^{\prime}_{\lambda/\mu}(q,t)\dfrac{c^{\prime}_{\lambda}(q,t)}{c^{\prime}_{\mu}(q,t)}\dfrac{1-t}{1-q}.$

(3.6)

The running index $\mu$ runs over the set of partitions such that $|\mu|=|\lambda|-1$ and $\mu\subset\lambda$.
card.label: Corollary 2.6

paper.title: Whittaker vector of deformed Virasoro algebra and Macdonald symmetric functions
paper.abstract: We give a proof of Awata and Yamada's conjecture for the explicit formula of Whittaker vector of the deformed Virasoro algebra realized in the Fock space. The formula is expressed as a summation over Macdonald symmetric functions with factored coefficients. In the proof we fully use currents appearing in the Fock representation of Ding-Iohara-Miki quantum algebra. We also mention an interpretation of Whittaker vector in terms of the geometry of the Hilbert schemes of points on the affine plane.
